claims.text: Describes Pons as the token launchpad on Robinhood Chain: launch a token in two steps and follow each launch as it raises, graduates and lists.
Says new tokens trade on a bonding curve until they graduate; its X says launches pair with supported assets on Uniswap v4 and earn creator fees.
Its X claims Pons accounts for about 16.7% of Robinhood Chain's cumulative DEX volume.
The site says Pons is noncustodial, tokens are issued by their creators, and Pons is not affiliated with Robinhood Markets.

aiView.text: Volume runs 2.8× liquidity across five pools, and FDV ranges $229M–$339M between pools, so the valuation depends on which pool is read. PONS is also the quote asset in an AI pool not counted here.

claims.text: Describes $CASHCAT as a memecoin honoring Robinhood's original name, Cash Cat, native to Robinhood Chain.
letscash.fun, linked from its site, says launched coins get permanently locked pools and the platform's cut buys back and burns CASHCAT.
Its X says CASHCAT was listed in the Robinhood app on Aug 6 and that perpetual futures went live on Coinbase and Deribit.

aiView.text: Volume runs 3× liquidity across two pools. The buyback-and-burn depends on letscash.fun activity, and that page itself reported degraded Robinhood Chain nodes at read time; the burn flow is not measured.

claims.text: Describes Artificial Inu as 'the onchain $NVDA community': a memecoin paired with tokenized NVDA stock.
Says every trade routes a cut into a community Vault holding NVDA, and fees collected in $AI are burned or locked permanently.
The site shows a Vault of 1,264.28 NVDA and 10,512 NVDA in liquidity pools; these are the site's figures.

aiView.text: The qualifying pools are quoted in PONS and USDG, so the NVDA pairing the site centres on is not among the pools this scan measured. Volume runs 3.6× liquidity.

claims.text: Its listed X is a self-described parody account ('Not actually Commander Vrax') that posts the contract and character memes.
Says the account replaced @VraxOnRobinhood, which it says was suspended after impersonation reports.
Search results (Phantom, CoinGape, DexTools) describe a Robinhood Chain cat-character memecoin; listings disagree on market cap.

aiView.text: Volume runs 4.5× liquidity in pools about 16 days old, and the only listed channel is an October-2026 parody account created after a suspension. No page describes token mechanics.

claims.text: Describes Hookr.fun as modular infrastructure for surfacing, composing and integrating custom Uniswap v4 hooks, live on Robinhood Chain.
Says pools combine 'Hook Blocks' such as anti-snipe caps, dynamic fees, auto-burn, LP rewards and arbitrage recapture; docs list an SDK and contracts.
The listed X belongs to Nodar, who describes himself as creator of DeFi Zaps and a former Zapper co-founder, now building Hookr.

aiView.text: One of few rows with developer docs and a named builder. Volume is only 1.4× liquidity, deeper than most rows; the text read does not explain how the HOOKR token captures hook fees.

claims.text: Its X presents $MEME, 'A Meme Coin', as an AMC-themed meme ('The theater was a front') and says it is paired with $AMC.
Its posts engage AMC CEO Adam Aron's objection to Robinhood creating AMC stock tokens without AMC's consent.

aiView.text: The X says it is paired with $AMC, but the only qualifying pool is quoted in WETH, and volume runs 16.7× that pool's liquidity, so price is fragile to modest trades.

gaps.reason: no website listed; the X names an AMC pairing but describes no other mechanics

claims.text: Describes The Standard Reserve as 'the sovereign onchain central bank' and a liquidity engine for onchain capital markets on Robinhood Chain.
Says traders swap tokens paired with $SPCX, $BABA and $SKHY through the Reserve's pools, and that burns outpace issuance with ~$1M put into buybacks.
Its X says King of the Markets, its launchpad and stock-token liquidity pilot, runs a rewards pool starting at 1M+ USDG.

aiView.text: Liquidity is about 10× daily volume, the inverse of most rows, which fits the X claim that the Reserve owns deep pools; ownership is not measured, and neither page read shows this contract.
